reviews.title: The Payment Wall
reviews.text:
The app’s biggest problem isn’t the subscription price—it’s the way the onboarding builds emotional investment before showing any real value.

I spent time personalizing my spiritual goals, expecting that to shape the experience, only to be met with a paywall before I could meaningfully use what I just set up. That makes the personalization feel manipulative instead of helpful.

The wording around “draw closer to God” next to a subscription price also comes across poorly. It unintentionally makes faith feel transactional, even if the actual intent is to charge for premium features.

A better experience would let users enter the personalized home page first, try a few free devotionals or guided prayers, and then offer premium as an enhancement.
